As of 300 PM EST Friday...

KEY MESSAGE 1...Above normal temperatures and tranquil weather 
through Saturday.

High pressure remains in control into Saturday, with dry conditions 
and above average temperatures expected. High clouds will be on the 
increase tonight into Saturday as an upper level trough approaches 
from the west and low pressure begins to develop off the Southeast 
coast. Cool again tonight with lows dropping back into the 30s 
inland and 40s closer to the coast. Similar temperatures are 
anticipated for Saturday with highs generally in the mid 60s to 
around 70F. 


KEY MESSAGE 2...Coastal low pressure brings increasing rain chances 
Sunday into Sunday night. While most areas will see measurable rain, 
confidence remains low regarding areal coverage of 0.5-1"+ rainfall 
amounts as there are still many differences in the models.

Attention remains focused on coastal low pressure developing off the 
Southeast coast this weekend before tracking northeastward offshore 
Sunday into Sunday night. Confidence in specifics remains low, as 
models have trended towards developing two separate low pressure 
centers, with heavier precipitation potentially splitting the area. 

The low pressure system currently over Florida is expected to track 
north toward the SE NC or SC coast before reaching the coastline by 
Saturday night-early Sunday morning. That low pressure center likely 
weakens while taking a track well inland through the NC and 
eventually VA Piedmont. Despite cool water temperatures, some (but 
certainly not all) of the models and ensemble members continue to 
insist on a secondary coastal low developing just east of the NC 
coast Saturday night before tracking north off the Mid-Atlantic 
coast on Sunday and eventually toward Long Island/Cape Cod by Monday 
So right now, forecast confidence is still lower than normal and we 
are looking at 3 possible scenarios being:

1. Coastal areas see 0.5-1"+ of rain with very little rain inland 
due to a secondary cyclogenesis just offshore of the VA/NC coast. 

2. The system making landfall in NC/SC maintains enough strength for 
areas along/west of I-95 to see 0.5-1"+ of rain with only scattered 
showers near the coast.

3. Only scattered showers with less than 0.5" of rain area-wide due 
to the secondary low developing way offshore or not at all while the 
inland system weakens substantially before arriving. 

The 12z HRRR, RRFS/REFS, and Canadian show very little in the way of 
secondary cyclogenesis offshore and are more optimistic with 
rainfall chances inland along the lines of scenario 2. The 06z 
ECMWF/EPS were more bullish on the low offshore of VA with much more 
rain near the immediate coast and favor scenario 1. On the other 
hand, the GEFS/GFS show the 2nd coastal low developing well offshore 
with very little precipitation inland as well. The latest 12z 
ECMWF/EPS has trended a bit toward scenario 2 with a bit more rain 
inland and less near the coast. So unfortunately for areas in 
drought, it is possible that we miss out on a significant wetting 
rain. Impacts wise, rain chances increase late Saturday into Sunday, 
with broad brush 80% PoPs due accounting for the inland/coastal 
scenarios. Rain chances diminish Sunday evening into Sunday night as 
the system exits. In addition to the rain, there could still also be 
a brief period of breezy NE to NW winds along the coast on Sunday if 
we see something close to scenario 1 above. Finally, given that the 
winds will likely be shifting and we will be coming out of the lower 
end of the astronomical high tide cycle, only minor tidal flooding 
is expected in the worst case scenario.


KEY MESSAGE 3...Drier conditions return early next week before 
another storm system potentially impacts the area by Thanksgiving. 

Low pressure continues tracking northeastward away from the area 
Monday. Any lingering precipitation, primarily over NE portions of 
the area, should gradually come to an end by Monday afternoon as the 
system departs. High pressure then builds into the region, with 
generally dry conditions favored into the middle of next week. After 
this, there is an increasing signal of some type of low pressure 
development by Wednesday or Thanksgiving along the frontal boundary 
south of the area. There is still quite a bit of variability with 
the 12z guidance with the GFS, ECMWF, and Canadian all showing 
differing solutions. This is still 5-6 days out and there will be 
plenty of time to pin down any details. However, given the +2 sigma 
high to the north, any low pressure to our south will lead to 
increased NE winds and the potential for some tidal flooding as we 
will be going into another King Tide cycle. Overall it seems like 
the Thanksgiving system will be more impactful than Sunday's storm, 
though rainfall amounts are uncertain.
